name: Multi-Session Chat
ontology_notes: Human-human friend chat over 3-5 sessions. Xu, Szlam, Weston, ACL 2022, arXiv 2107.07567. Crowdworkers play PersonaChat personas. Sessions are 6-7 turns per speaker. Simulated gaps of 1-7 hours or 1-7 days. Annotators write summaries of important personal points between sessions (extended personas). Train has 4,000 episodes with 3 sessions and 1,001 with 4. Valid/test go to 5 sessions (~66 utterances). Task lives at parlai/tasks/msc. Metrics in the paper are perplexity, human eval, and session-opening quality. Not a fact-QA memory leaderboard.

supersession.evidence: Summaries accumulate personal points. The paper does not score replacing an old fact with a newer contradictory one.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Sessions are separated by simulated hours or days. Opening turns are written as catching up after that gap. That is the public bench closest to a time skip. Gaps are hours or days, not three months, and there is no dated-fact QA.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: Each worker has a persona plus growing summaries about self and partner. Two peers, not user vs companion character vs lore.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: No abstention or 'do not recall' items. Crowdworkers are told to use past personal details.
silence.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: Summaries are additive extended personas. No forget-that.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Paper reports perplexity and human judgments. Table 3 tracks truncation. That is context-window pressure, not cost per companion turn vs session count.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: ParlAI MIT. parlai display_data -t msc and eval_model commands on the project page run locally once ParlAI and the zoo models are installed.
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Ancestor of multi-session friend chat and the only common bench with an explicit between-session time skip. Five sessions and perplexity/human next-utterance scoring will not select a companion memory system.

published_eval.name: Multi-Session Chat (MSC)
published_eval.claimed_score: Paper. Retrieval-augmented and summary-memory models beat truncated encoder-decoders on perplexity and human eval. SumMem-MSC 2.7B FiD-RAG is the project-page headline zoo model. Session openings show about 2 perplexity points difference with vs without previous-session context (Table 4 discussion).
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Next-utterance quality in human-human multi-session chit-chat, especially reopenings after a simulated hours-or-days gap, with optional gold or predicted summaries as memory.

open_unknowns: stars_observed is ParlAI's repo star count, not a standalone MSC repo.
Dataset license is inherited from ParlAI MIT unless a task file says otherwise. Not separately audited in this pass.
